text: From a functional standpoint, individual skeletal muscles are generally considered single entities. However, the structure of muscle is highly complex. Muscle is surrounded by layers of connective tissue. The outer layer covering the entire muscle is called the epimysium ; within the whole muscle are small bundles of fibers called fasciculi that are encased in the perimy- sium ; and within the fasciculus are individual muscle cells (i.e., fibers) covered by sheaths of endomysium . The number of fibers ranges from several hundred in the small muscles of the eardrum to over a million in large muscles such as the gastrocnemius.
